detail.body:
## Summary

- route rope-free sparse MLA to the ROCm Triton implementation for every KV-cache dtype
- dequantize FP8 KV rows in the Triton ragged-prefill kernel using the layer KV scale while keeping Q in model dtype
- use 64-bit query-row offsets so wide, long-context prefills cannot overflow 32-bit pointer arithmetic
- preserve custom MLA geometry and FP8 cache dtype in the attention benchmark harness

## Problem

AITER precompiled sparse MLA kernels assume the DeepSeek cache-row geometry: 512 latent elements plus 64 RoPE elements. GLM-5.3-Flash is rope-free and stores a 512-element row. FP8 NoPE requests currently reach the AITER path, whose 576-element assumption can read past the cache row and cause a ROCm GPU memory fault.

The existing Triton ragged path already handles the NoPE geometry. This change makes its routing geometry-based instead of BF16-only, adds scaled FP8 KV dequantization, and avoids FP8-quantizing Q for that path.

## Duplicate-work check

No open PR found addresses ROCm NoPE FP8 sparse-attention KV rows. #39168 overlaps the ROCm ops file but changes the separate FP8 indexer-cache MQA path; the open GLM-5.3 NoPE FP8 PRs target NVIDIA backends. The previously bundled SharedTopkIndicesBuffer no-op was dropped because #57252 already landed ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl.record_logical_topk_ready().

## Validation

Rebased onto main@63d9ad0a. Head: ae5cad3d.

Hardware validation used a full ROCm wheel from the previous head (73860da5) on the GLM-5.3-specific ROCm base image. The rebase kept the same kernel/backend/benchmark hunks and only resolved a header-constant conflict with the new upstream FP8_DTYPE plus dropped the now-redundant top-k no-op.

- pytest -q tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_glm5next_sparse.py: **23 passed** on the pre-rebase validated image
- FP8 sparse MLA attention sweep: **24/24 shapes passed**
- TP=4 GLM-5.3-Flash FP8 serving matrix: **20/20 points passed, 1,360/1,360 requests succeeded**
- post-rebase: ruff check and ruff format --check pass on all 5 changed files; git diff --check clean; files py_compile clean

The serving matrix used `--max-num-batched-tokens 131072 --no-enable-chunked-prefill` so each long prompt exercises the full-query FP8 MLA path. During diagnosis, default partial chunking on current main showed a separate GPU fault only after all instrumented sparse indexer and attention calls had synchronized and returned; it reproduced across both generic-nightly and GLM-specific runtime bases and is outside this FP8 MLA kernel change.

## GSM8K

Same recipe as other GLM-5.3-Flash PRs (#57590, #56960, #56176, #55738, #54925): EleutherAI `lm_eval` against `/v1/completions`, 5-shot, greedy. Not chat completions.

```
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 vllm serve .../GLM-5.3-Flash \
    --tensor-parallel-size 4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
    --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_MLA_SPARSE --max-num-seqs 64

lm_eval --model local-completions \
  --model_args model=glm53,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:9610/v1/completions,tokenizer=.../GLM-5.3-Flash,num_concurrent=64,tokenized_requests=False \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --batch_size 1 --gen_kwargs temperature=0 --seed 12345
```

`gen_kwargs`: `until=['Question:', '</s>', '<|im_end|>']`, `do_sample=False`, `temperature=0` (lm_eval gsm8k.yaml defaults). Full 1,319 questions. No GPU faults.

| Filter | n-shot | Metric | Value | Stderr |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|
| flexible-extract | 5 | exact_match | **0.9158** | ± 0.0076 |
| strict-match | 5 | exact_match | **0.9158** | ± 0.0076 |

That matches the published GLM-5.3-Flash `lm_eval` completions band: #54925 0.9158 / 0.9143 (model card 0.9128), #56176 0.9121 BF16 / 0.9219 MXFP4, #57546 0.9174 / 0.9166, #56960 0.9249 / 0.9234, #55738 93.03% ± 0.70.

## Serving performance (BF16 KV vs FP8 KV)

`vllm bench serve` random dataset, same recipe as ROCm GLM-5.3-Flash PRs #57590 / #57979 (and NVIDIA #55736): `--backend vllm --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8000 --random-output-len 1000 --random-range-ratio 0 --ignore-eos --seed 5678 --num-prompts $((8*CONC)) --num-warmups $CONC`. Each point was run 3 times; the table shows the median of the 3 runs' median TPOT, output tok/s and median TTFT.

Head 291fe72f80, with this PR's Python tree overlaid on `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-81198e97` (main including #58584). Both arms use this build, so FP8 and BF16 decode both go through the split-K kernel. Baseline is **BF16 KV** (main cannot boot FP8 NoPE). TP=4 on MI355X, `--attention-backend ROCM_AITER_MLA_SPARSE --max-model-len 16384 --max-num-seqs 64 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --no-enable-prefix-caching`. 24/24 runs, 2,736/2,736 requests succeeded.

| ISL/OSL | conc | BF16 TPOT ms | FP8 TPOT ms | TPOT Δ | BF16 tok/s | FP8 tok/s | tok/s Δ | BF16 TTFT ms | FP8 TTFT ms | TTFT Δ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 8000/1000 | 1 | 8.75 | 8.76 | +0.2% | 111.0 | 110.9 | -0.1% | 262 | 261 | -0.5% |
| 8000/1000 | 8 | 11.36 | 11.33 | -0.3% | 639.2 | 640.4 | +0.2% | 1159 | 1160 | +0.1% |
| 8000/1000 | 16 | 15.78 | 15.74 | -0.2% | 919.8 | 918.9 | -0.1% | 1632 | 1831 | +12.2% |
| 8000/1000 | 32 | 20.41 | 20.35 | -0.3% | 1444.7 | 1446.8 | +0.1% | 1849 | 1860 | +0.6% |

FP8 TPOT and throughput are within 0.3% of BF16 at every concurrency. The c=16 TTFT delta comes from queueing, not from the kernel: the 16 concurrent 8k prompts fill the 16k-token prefill budget about two at a time, so the median request lands on one of two prefill waves. Both arms hit both values across identical repeats (BF16 1628 / 1821 / 1628 ms, FP8 1599 / 1831 / 1831 ms).

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used to investigate, implement, test, rebase, and prepare this change.

+def _sparse_attn_fp32_reference(q, kv, indices, indptr, scale, attn_sink):
+    q = q.float()
+    out = torch.zeros_like(q)
+    for row in range(q.shape[0]):

@simondanielsson Yes, for this model that's expected, and it isn't dequant overhead. FP8 does make the attention kernel faster; attention is just a small share of a GLM-5.3-Flash decode step:

- Sparse top-k caps each query at 2,048 KV rows regardless of context length. The 512-wide latent is shared by every head (MQA), so a decode token reads about 2 MB of KV per layer in BF16 and 1 MB in FP8. That doesn't grow with the 8k context.
- Split-K decode kernel on MI355X, TP=4 per-rank shapes (16 heads, top-k 2,048):

| decode tokens per rank | BF16 µs | FP8 µs | FP8 / BF16 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 27.7 | 27.6 | 0.99 |
| 8 | 26.5 | 27.7 | 1.05 |
| 16 | 31.3 | 26.8 | 0.86 |
| 32 | 45.5 | 34.2 | 0.75 |

- Across 45 layers, the best case is about 0.2 ms of the 15.8 ms TPOT at c=16 (about 1%) and 0.5 ms of 20.4 ms at c=32 (about 2.5%). At c=1–8 the kernel is latency-bound, so FP8 doesn't help. The measured TPOT gain was 0.2–0.3%, so not all of the kernel-level gain shows up end to end. I haven't profiled where the rest goes, so I won't claim more than that.
- The c=16 "worse" number is TTFT, not TPOT. It comes from prefill queueing; see the per-repetition values under the table in the description.

The main benefit of FP8 KV here is capacity: half the KV memory per token, so roughly twice the cached tokens or concurrency for the same memory.
